basis.governing_question: How can Vale Verde Water Company lose less treated water through leaks in its network, starting with two pilot districts?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish how much treated water the network loses and where, as the baseline for the loss-reduction program.

gate.label: Diagnostic sign-off
gate.decision: Does the steering group accept the loss baseline as the basis for the program design?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the loss-reduction program and the new leak-detection routine, and plan the pilot in two districts.

gate.label: Go/no-go on pilot
gate.decision: Does the steering group approve the program design and the pilot in two districts?

phases.name: Pilot
phases.objective_one_line: Run the new leak-detection routine in two districts and measure water losses against their pre-pilot level.

gate.label: Go/no-go on rollout
gate.decision: Do the pilot results in two districts justify rolling the program out to the others?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Roll out the leak-detection routine to the remaining districts so every district runs it by the end.

gate.label: Rollout completion
gate.decision: Is the new routine running in every district, so measurement can start?

phases.name: Measurement
phases.objective_one_line: Track water losses and routine adoption against the two success criteria, and report the results.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Does the steering group accept the measured results as the final result?

workstreams.name: Network water balance
workstreams.answers: How much treated water does the network lose today, and how much of that is leakage?
activities: Collect operational data on water supplied and consumed
Review network documents and existing loss reporting
Interview operations staff on how losses are measured

workstreams.name: Loss locations and causes
workstreams.answers: In which districts and parts of the network do the losses occur, and what drives them?
activities: Compare supplied and consumed water district by district
Interview maintenance crews on where and why leaks occur
Review available repair records and network documents

workstreams.name: Program and routine design
workstreams.answers: What does the loss-reduction program consist of, and how should the new leak-detection routine work day to day?
activities: Draft the leak-detection routine, its steps and roles
Define program targets and measures against the baseline
Test the draft routine with field crews

workstreams.name: Pilot plan
workstreams.answers: How will the two pilot districts be chosen, prepared and measured against their pre-pilot level of losses?
activities: Set selection criteria for the two pilot districts
Define how pilot losses are compared with pre-pilot levels
Plan the pilot schedule, crew needs and readiness checks

workstreams.name: Pilot readiness
workstreams.answers: Are the two pilot districts, their crews and their data ready for the new routine to start?
activities: Train crews in the two pilot districts on the new routine
Set up district data collection for leak and loss records
Check readiness with the crews who will run the routine

workstreams.name: Pilot loss measurement
workstreams.answers: How do water losses in the two pilot districts compare with their level before the pilot?
activities: Establish each pilot district's pre-pilot loss level
Track district water balance through the pilot weeks
Compare pilot results with pre-pilot levels for the gate

workstreams.name: Pilot operation
workstreams.answers: What happens when crews run the new leak-detection routine in the two districts for several weeks?
activities: Run the routine in the two pilot districts
Log leaks found, repairs made and time to repair
Review progress weekly with district crews

workstreams.name: Rollout readiness
workstreams.answers: How should the routine, training and district order be adjusted for rollout, based on the pilot findings?
activities: Review pilot findings with the crews who ran the routine
Sequence the remaining districts into rollout waves
Prepare training material for the remaining districts

workstreams.name: Crew training and coaching
workstreams.answers: Can district crews run the routine on their own once each wave goes live?
activities: Train district crews before their wave goes live
Coach crews on site in the first weeks of each wave
Observe routine use and gather crew feedback

workstreams.name: District rollout
workstreams.answers: How does the routine go live in each remaining district, and what do the first waves show?
activities: Bring the routine live in each wave of districts
Record leaks found and repairs made in each district
Review wave results and adjust the next wave

workstreams.name: Loss and adoption tracking
workstreams.answers: What do water losses in the two pilot districts and routine use in all districts show against the baseline?
activities: Track pilot district losses against their pre-pilot level
Check routine use in every district from operational data
Interview district crews on what changed in their work

workstreams.name: Results readout
workstreams.answers: Do the measured results meet both success criteria, and what explains them?
activities: Test results against both success criteria
Check results for other causes of changes in losses
Write the results report for the final readout

deliverables.name: Network water balance and leakage share
Loss baseline by district, with locations and causes
Leak-detection routine with steps and roles
Pilot plan with district selection and measurement method
Crew training record and pilot readiness check
Pre-pilot loss levels for the two districts
Pilot results against pre-pilot loss levels
Pilot go-live record and operation log, two districts
Rollout wave plan and training material
Crew training and coaching record by wave
First-wave results report from the district rollout
Go-live record for each remaining district
Loss and routine-use tracker against the baseline
Results report for the final readout

events.label: Kick-off
events.decision: Does the steering group confirm the scope, team and calendar for the engagement?
agenda: Present the five phases and what each one delivers
Align on team roles and who attends each steering meeting
Confirm the steering meeting dates and the network data needed from week 1

events.label: Check-in: water balance
events.purpose: Review water balance and leakage share
events.decision: Does the water balance need any adjustment before the loss baseline is finalized?
agenda: Present the network water balance and leakage share
Discuss figures that need adjusting before the baseline
Confirm next steps toward the loss baseline

events.label: Diagnostic sign-off
events.purpose: Close the Diagnostic on the loss baseline
events.decision: Does the steering group accept the loss baseline as the basis for the program design?
agenda: Present the loss baseline by district with locations and causes
Review the water balance and leakage share behind it
Decide whether the baseline is the basis for the program design

events.label: Check-in: design basis
events.decision: Do the routine and program targets stand as the basis for the pilot plan?
agenda: Present the leak-detection routine with its steps and roles
Review the loss-reduction program targets and measures
Confirm what the pilot plan builds on in the weeks ahead

events.label: Go/no-go on pilot
events.purpose: Decide on program design and pilot start
events.decision: Does the steering group approve the program design and the pilot in two districts?
agenda: Present the pilot plan with district selection and measurement method
Review the routine design and the program targets
Decide on the program design and the pilot in two districts

events.label: Workshop 1: pilot readiness
events.purpose: Review readiness before the pilot goes live
events.decision: Is the pilot ready to go live in the two districts?
agenda: Present the crew training record and readiness check
Review pre-pilot loss levels for the two districts
Confirm the go-live arrangements for the two districts

events.label: Go/no-go on rollout
events.purpose: Decide on rollout from pilot results
events.decision: Do the pilot results in two districts justify rolling the program out to the others?
agenda: Present the pilot results against pre-pilot loss levels
Review the go-live record and operation log for the two districts
Decide whether the program rolls out to the other districts

events.label: Workshop 2: wave readiness
events.purpose: Review readiness before the first wave
events.decision: Is the rollout ready to go live in the first wave of districts?
agenda: Present the rollout wave plan and training material
Review the order of the waves and what each wave needs
Confirm the conditions for first-wave go-live

events.label: Workshop 3: wave results
events.purpose: Review first-wave results before more waves
events.decision: Should the remaining waves proceed as planned, given the first-wave results?
agenda: Present the first-wave results report from the district rollout
Discuss lessons for training and coaching in later waves
Confirm the plan for the remaining districts

events.label: Rollout completion
events.purpose: Close the rollout on go-live records
events.decision: Is the new routine running in every district, so measurement can start?
agenda: Present the go-live record for each remaining district
Review the crew training and coaching record by wave
Decide whether the routine runs in every district

events.label: Check-in: loss tracking
events.decision: Does the tracker cover both success criteria well enough for the results report?
agenda: Present the loss and routine-use tracker against the baseline
Review loss and adoption figures against the two success criteria
Confirm what the results report needs to cover

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Close the engagement on measured results
events.decision: Does the steering group accept the measured results as the final result?
agenda: Present the results report for the final readout
Review loss and routine use against the baseline
Decide whether the measured results are accepted as final

architect_notes: The brief's 'rollout' stage is named Implementation as the closest fit; confirm whether the firm executes the rollout or the client does.
Departs from performance_improvement: adds Design, Pilot and Measurement phases because the brief names five stages.
